assumptions: A single local user runs notewell from a terminal against notes they own.
Notes are UTF-8 Markdown; binary and non-.md files are skipped silently.
The first release ships lexical ranking only, as the draft requires.

decisions.title: Single-file inverted index in the user cache directory
decisions.context: The draft forbids a database server and requires a rebuildable index that is safe to delete.
decisions.decision: Persist one JSON inverted index under the platform user cache directory, written atomically through a temporary file and rename.
consequences: Deleting the index file is always safe; the next index run rebuilds it.
The whole index is loaded into memory, which bounds the supported corpus size.

decisions.title: Field-weighted term-frequency ranking
decisions.context: Body-only term frequency ranks long notes above short, precisely titled ones.
decisions.decision: Score each note by term frequency with titles and headings weighted above body text, and break ties by newest modification time.
consequences: Ranking needs the parser to keep heading structure, not just a token stream.
No embeddings or external ranking service are required.

phases.name: Index core
phases.objective: Parse Markdown notes and persist a rebuildable on-disk index incrementally.
exitCriteria: Indexing a directory twice re-reads only changed files.
Deleting the index file and re-indexing reproduces the same index contents.

phases.name: Query and CLI
phases.objective: Answer ranked and tag-filtered queries from the persisted index through a CLI.
exitCriteria: search returns ranked results with path, title, and one matching line.

tasks.title: Create the strict TypeScript scaffold and parse Markdown notes
tasks.objective: Create the npm and strict-TypeScript project scaffold, then read a .md file and produce a document with its title, headings, body tokens, front-matter tags, and modification time.
acceptanceCriteria: The task creates package.json with test, typecheck, and build scripts plus the future notewell executable entry, and creates package-lock.json from the installed development dependencies.
The task creates tsconfig.json with strict TypeScript enabled and .gitignore excluding node_modules, build output, DraftForge run artifacts, upgrade backups, and config.local.json.
YAML front matter delimited by --- yields a tag list.
A note without front matter parses with an empty tag list.
Headings are retained separately from body text, with parser behavior covered under test/parse/.
exclusions: No filesystem walking and no index persistence.

tasks.title: Build and persist the inverted index incrementally
tasks.objective: Walk a notes directory, index parsed documents, and persist the index atomically, re-reading only files whose size or mtime changed.
acceptanceCriteria: A second index run over an unchanged directory reads no note files.
A deleted index file is rebuilt on the next run.
An interrupted write never leaves a partial index in place.
Incremental indexing and atomic persistence are covered under test/index/.
exclusions: No query evaluation and no CLI wiring.

tasks.title: Rank query matches against the persisted index
tasks.objective: Evaluate a term query over the index and return notes ordered by field-weighted score, newest first on ties.
acceptanceCriteria: A title match outranks an equal-frequency body match.
Equal scores order by newest modification time.
Tag filtering restricts results to notes carrying the tag.
Ranking and filtering behavior are covered under test/query/.
exclusions: No output formatting and no argument parsing.

tasks.title: Expose the index and search commands
tasks.objective: Wire the index and query layers behind notewell index and notewell search, including --tag.
acceptanceCriteria: search prints path, title, and one matching line per result.
search --tag passes the filter through to the query layer.
A query with no matches exits 0 and prints no results.
CLI argument and output behavior are covered under test/cli/.
exclusions: No changes to parsing, indexing, or ranking behavior.

risks.description: An interrupted index write could corrupt the single index file.
risks.mitigation: Write to a temporary file in the same directory and rename atomically.

risks.description: Size and mtime comparison misses same-size edits within one timestamp granularity.
risks.mitigation: Record a content hash alongside size and mtime and compare it when the timestamp is ambiguous.
